title: Improve soft-throttle queue aging with kernel-selection hints and KV prefetch for continuous-batcher
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Context: production traffic patterns show intermittent starvation of small, latency-sensitive requests when the continuous-batcher aggregates large inflight KV-heavy requests. Motivation: reduce p95 tail and avoid unfair queuing without sacrificing batching efficiency or adding hard preemption. This PR introduces a soft-throttle queue-aging mechanism combined with per-request kernel-selection hints and an opportunistic KV prefetch path. Design summary: 1) Soft-throttle aging: requests accrue an aging score while queued; the admission controller uses a decaying soft-reservation that elevates aged requests' priority to break starvation while capping the extra reservation to avoid loss of batch efficiency. 2) Kernel-selection hints: the runtime exposes a lightweight hint (hint.kernel_preference) derived from predicted sequence-length distribution and token-type info. The scheduler uses this hint to preferentially co-locate requests with compatible kernel targets, reducing kernel-switch overhead inside a batch. 3) KV prefetch micro-path: for requests marked as KV-prefetchable, we add a non-blocking prefetch into the KV cache during queuing windows; prefetches are rate-limited by a token bucket per GPU to avoid cache thrash. Implementation notes: - Admission scorer updated in continuous-batcher/admission.cc to track per-request aging_score and soft_reserve_pct (defaults: 12% max uplift, half-life 8s). - Kernel hints flow added at the API layer (serving/proto/request.proto) and plumbed to the scheduler with minimal serialization overhead. - KV prefetch implemented in kv_cache/prefetch.h and invoked by the batcher when a request's hint.kv_prefetch==true. Prefetch uses existing kv-async interfaces and increments an internal prefetch-miss metric to detect ineffective prefetches. Default config changes (runtime flags): --batcher.soft_reserve_pct_max=12 --batcher.soft_reserve_half_life=8s --kv.prefetch_rate_per_gpu=20/s --scheduler.kernel_hint_merge_window=7ms Testing and results: - Unit & integration: added 12 unit tests and 4 integration flows covering aging score transitions, hint propagation, and prefetch backpressure. - Benchmarks (internal lab, A100, mixed toy workload): median latency for small chat requests (<=64 tokens) decreased by 6%, p95 decreased by 22% under mixed load, and overall token throughput was stable (+0.8% measured variance within noise). - Real traffic canary (10% of us-west-2 traffic for 48h): observed 19% fewer latency incidents (alerts crossing 200ms) and no KV cache churn increase beyond expected. Rollout plan: staged canary starting at 5% -> 10% -> 50% with automated rollback on >3% increase in 95th percentile or >1.5x prefetch-miss growth. Monitoring: new metrics emitted: batcher.soft_reserve_uplift, scheduler.kernel_hint_cohort_hits, kv.prefetch_miss_ratio. Backwards compatibility: kernel hint defaults to unset; behavior unchanged unless clients opt into hints or rollout toggles turned on. Risk analysis: main risk is over-prefetching causing KV cache eviction; mitigations: per-GPU rate limits, incremental canary, and metric-based rollback. Misc: added doc string comments in proto and runtime config; preserved feature flags for quick disable.

review_comments: Liam: Can you justify the 12% default uplift? What was the sensitivity analysis?

Priya: 12% is conservative; we swept in lab from 0-25% and observed diminishing returns beyond 15% and batch efficiency drop >6% after 20% (bench numbers summarized in PR description). Chosen for safety during canary.
Ava: The kernel_hint enum looks fine but ensure forward compatibility if we add more kernel targets. Consider making it extensible (string-based) in the long term.
Priya: Agreed; added comment in proto and feature flag to make migration easier. We'll follow up with an RFC for string identifiers if we add >3 targets.
Diego: KV prefetch backpressure—what if prefetches themselves evict warm keys? How do we detect that?
Priya: We emit kv.prefetch_miss_ratio and kv.prefetch_eviction_delta; canary thresholds will alert on >1.5x. We also lower prefetch rate automatically if miss_ratio climbs beyond 0.2.
Liam: CI flaky on integration; please re-run after fix. (marked as required)
Priya: Re-ran CI after adjusting a timing assert; integration now stable.

release_notes: Introduce soft-throttle queue-aging to reduce starvation for latency-sensitive requests, add kernel-selection hints to improve kernel co-location within batches, and optional opportunistic KV prefetching during queueing. Configurable flags allow tuning of uplift, half-life, merge window, and prefetch rate. Backwards compatible by default.
